name: Managed Redis
summary: Redis that you cannot reach directly, such as a managed cloud Redis: down, memory, clients, command time, evictions, rejected connections and restarts.
needs: A Grafana instance whose Prometheus datasource holds redis_exporter series (redis_up, redis_memory_used_bytes, ...), or the same series under another prefix.

placeholders.label: Grafana
placeholders.help: The Grafana instance whose datasource holds the Redis series.

placeholders.label: Datasource
placeholders.help: The name or uid of the Grafana Prometheus datasource that holds the Redis series.

placeholders.label: Name
placeholders.help: A short name for these Redis instances in the check names and ids, such as cache-prod.

placeholders.label: Selector
placeholders.help: Optional label matchers that pick the Redis series, such as env="prod". Empty reads every Redis series in the datasource.

placeholders.label: Metric prefix
placeholders.help: The start of every Redis metric name: redis_ for redis_exporter (redis_up, redis_connected_clients, ...). Change it only when your metrics are renamed.

placeholders.label: Instance label
placeholders.help: The label that names each Redis instance in the series.

checks.name: Redis ${name} down
checks.title: {${label}} down
checks.text: Redis {${label}} is down: ${prefix}up is 0, so its exporter cannot reach it. Clients that need it fail or fall back to their source.

checks.name: Redis ${name} memory
checks.query: 100 * max by (${label}) (max_over_time(${prefix}memory_used_bytes{${selector}}[30m])) / max by (${label}) (${prefix}memory_max_bytes{${selector}}) < 95 and on (${label}) (max by (${label}) (${prefix}up{${selector}}) >= 0.5)
checks.title: {${label}} memory at {value} %
checks.text: Redis {${label}} peaked at {value} % of its memory limit in the last 30 min. Near the limit, writes fail or keys get evicted, depending on the eviction policy; find the keys that grow (big caches without a TTL) before it fills.

checks.name: Redis ${name} memory critical
checks.query: 100 * max by (${label}) (max_over_time(${prefix}memory_used_bytes{${selector}}[30m])) / max by (${label}) (${prefix}memory_max_bytes{${selector}}) and on (${label}) (max by (${label}) (${prefix}up{${selector}}) >= 0.5)
checks.title: {${label}} memory at {value} %
checks.text: Redis {${label}} peaked at {value} % of its memory limit in the last 30 min. Near the limit, writes fail or keys get evicted, depending on the eviction policy; find the keys that grow (big caches without a TTL) before it fills.

checks.name: Redis ${name} clients
checks.query: 100 * max by (${label}) (max_over_time(${prefix}connected_clients{${selector}}[30m])) / max by (${label}) (${prefix}config_maxclients{${selector}}) and on (${label}) (max by (${label}) (${prefix}up{${selector}}) >= 0.5)
checks.title: {${label}} clients at {value} % of the limit
checks.text: Redis {${label}} peaked at {value} % of its client limit (maxclients) in the last 30 min. A full limit refuses new connections, so pods that start or scale out cannot reach Redis.

checks.name: Redis ${name} command time
checks.query: (1e6 * sum by (${label}) (increase(${prefix}commands_duration_seconds_total{${selector}}[30m])) / sum by (${label}) (increase(${prefix}commands_processed_total{${selector}}[30m])) >= 3 * max by (${label}) (label_replace(1e6 * sum by (${label}) (increase(${prefix}commands_duration_seconds_total{${selector}}[30m] offset 1d)) / sum by (${label}) (increase(${prefix}commands_processed_total{${selector}}[30m] offset 1d)), "base", "1d", "", "") or label_replace(1e6 * sum by (${label}) (increase(${prefix}commands_duration_seconds_total{${selector}}[30m] offset 7d)) / sum by (${label}) (increase(${prefix}commands_processed_total{${selector}}[30m] offset 7d)), "base", "7d", "", ""))) and on (${label}) (max by (${label}) (${prefix}up{${selector}}) >= 0.5)
checks.title: {${label}} command time {value} us
checks.text: Redis {${label}} averaged {value} us per command in the last 30 min, at least 3 times the same 30 min 1 day or 1 week earlier. Redis runs commands on one thread, so slow commands (KEYS, big SCANs, large values) queue everything behind them.

checks.name: Redis ${name} evictions
checks.title: {${label}} evicted {value} keys
checks.text: Redis {${label}} reported {value} evicted keys in the last 30 min: memory is full and Redis is dropping cached data.

checks.name: Redis ${name} rejected connections
checks.title: {${label}} rejected {value} connections
checks.text: Redis {${label}} reported {value} rejected connections in the last 30 min: the client limit was hit.

checks.name: Redis ${name} restart
checks.title: {${label}} restarted
checks.text: Redis {${label}} has been up for only {value} s: it restarted, so clients reconnected and an in-memory cache may start cold.

checks.name: Redis ${name} no series
checks.title: no Redis series for ${name}
checks.text: The selector of the Managed Redis preset for ${name} matches no ${prefix}up series in the datasource, so every other check of this preset is quiet: check the selector, the metric prefix and the datasource.
